info.name: Server Moderation Session Service
info.description:
Team 16 - "Student ID, please". Server Moderation Session Service, owner Postoronca Dumitru.

Every request name carries the status code it expects, so the collection can be checked mechanically. Folders marked 'run in order' capture ids into collection variables and depend on the requests before them - use the Collection Runner on the folder rather than firing individual requests.

Order: health -> auth -> caller identity -> sessions (contract) -> events - decision.recorded comes from the broker -> ending the shift -> errors - setup -> error codes -> sessions (beyond contract) -> dev - task timeout -> cleanup.

Every request goes through the Gateway, except the DIRECT CALLS below. Requests that act for a player send `Authorization: Bearer <jwt>`; the 'auth' folder registers four fresh players through Player Service (POST /player/players), logs them in and stores their ids and tokens, so run it first. Fresh players keep the run independent of the seed - the seeded dima_mod, maxim_jr and vlad_jr are members of the seeded active session, the contract's own example - and of the other collections; the cleanup folder deletes them. The Gateway validates the token and forwards only `X-Player-Id`.

DIRECT CALLS. The Lab 4 Gateway serves only the client routes (README "Gateway") and answers 404 on every other path. These go to one instance directly through {{session_direct_url}}, with the instance's own paths: GET /health/ready, GET /status, GET /logs, GET /metrics, GET /api/v1/sessions/{id}/deliveries, PUT /api/v1/sessions/{id} (the 405, with X-Player-Id) and GET /api/v1/dev/slow. GET /logs and /deliveries send `X-Service-Token: {{service_token}}`, which must equal SERVICE_TOKEN in the CPR .env. POST /session/events stays on the Gateway to show that no client can push an event.

LAB 4 (4.0.0). decision.recorded arrives from the Message Broker (topic events.decision.recorded), not on POST /events, which is removed; the service's calls to Player, Server Rules and Applicant go through the broker too, so the flow needs those services on the broker: Server Rules, Applicant and Player run 4.0.0 in the CPR compose; or run the session without MESSAGE_BROKER_URL, on its stubs. Postman cannot send the broker's gRPC calls: publish decision.recorded with the broker's scripts/smoke.py (docs/SERVER_MODERATION_SESSION_SERVICE.md, §11).

Set `base_url` if the Gateway is not on http://localhost:8080. The player ids are captured at registration.

Full reference: docs/SERVER_MODERATION_SESSION_SERVICE.md in the Common Public Repository.

caller identity
item.description:
Proves how this service decides which player a request acts for, without creating anything: each request either fails authentication outright, or gets past it to a Player Service lookup that 404s. Safe to run at any point.

The Gateway validates `Authorization: Bearer <jwt>`, removes it and forwards the player id as `X-Player-Id`; the service reads that header and nothing else, and validates no token. The 401s here therefore come from the Gateway.

request.description: 401 rather than 400: the request is well formed, it simply says nothing about who is making it - which is the status a real token check would return too.

item.name: a token that is not a JWT -> 401 UNAUTHENTICATED (Gateway)

request.description: A token present but unusable is refused by the Gateway with 401 before the request reaches the service; the Gateway never forwards an X-Player-Id it could not take from a valid token.
Only the Bearer scheme is accepted (case-insensitively, per RFC 7235).

request.description: A new applicant is given only when the current one already has a decision. item.name: events - decision.recorded comes from the broker (Lab 4)
item.description: From 4.0.0 decision.recorded is delivered by the Message Broker (topic events.decision.recorded) and settled with Ack; POST /events is removed from the instance, and the Lab 4 Gateway does not serve POST /events at all. Postman cannot send gRPC: publish it with the broker's scripts/smoke.py (docs/SERVER_MODERATION_SESSION_SERVICE.md, §11 'prove a decision is applied only once'), then read its effect with GET /sessions/{id} and GET /sessions/{id}/decisions.

item.name: POST /session/events through the Gateway -> 404 NOT_FOUND (not a client route; events arrive from the broker)

request.description: Shows that no client can push an event: the Lab 4 Gateway answers 404 on POST /events itself, before any credential check, and sends nothing to the broker. The instance no longer has the route either (4.0.0); decision.recorded arrives on its subscription to events.decision.recorded.

item.name: ending the shift and the outbox
item.description: Ending the shift freezes the per-player result and writes session.ended. The event goes to an outbox table in the same transaction as the state change, with one delivery to the Message Broker, and the relay publishes it to events.session.ended (4.0.0) - the events endpoint is how you prove that what this service produces is what Player Service expects to receive.

request.description: The Moderator ends the shift. Session works out the final score, penalties, XP for every player and any disciplinary actions, freezes them and writes session.ended. An applicant still undecided is dropped and does not count.

request.description: A malformed id is a client bug. Reporting it as 404 would hide that behind a legitimate-looking answer.

The contract says a player's request carries their JWT and the endpoint takes player_id from it. Player Service issues that JWT; without one the Gateway answers 401 itself and the request never reaches the service.

request.description: Run the 'errors - setup' folder first: junior_a is in the pair lobby it opens. A player in a lobby or an active session cannot open another. A player whose last shift has ENDED can - which is why this uses junior_a rather than the moderator, whose session finished two folders ago.
Run the 'errors - setup' request first to get a fresh lobby. Only the creator may start a session.
The solo lobby from the setup folder. A shift needs a Moderator and at least one Junior Moderator.
The contract fixes three statuses and no others.
A typo in a query string is rejected rather than ignored, so it does not silently return the first page.
Even routing failures use the shared error envelope.

The instance's own 405. Through the Gateway a known path with a method it does not take answers 404 (README "Gateway"), so it goes to one instance directly, with X-Player-Id as the Gateway would set it.
